thesis_points: First publicly traded land banking REIT — 876 communities, 139,000 homesites, $8.4B homesite inventory under option

Other Agreements segment growing 3.4x from Q1–Q3 2025 — rapidly diversifying beyond Lennar's ~80% revenue share
IROIC (9.5–10.3%) exceeds WACC; value-accretive at current P/BV of ~0.87x; book value grows as inventory expands
HOPP'R technology platform (centralized land analytics + deal execution) creates a moat difficult to replicate at scale
Consensus analyst: 'Land is land — unless there's a recession, no reason to trade at a discount to book'

key_debate.street: Lennar concentration risk (80% revenue); limited operating history makes walkaway risk difficult to price; housing macro headwinds

overview.narrative:
REITs posted broad gains on Monday with hospitality leading all subsectors at +2.77% on average, powered by INN's +4.20% move as leisure travel demand data continues to firm heading into the summer booking season. Tower REITs followed at +1.81%, anchored by AMT's +3.90% surge, likely reflecting renewed investor appetite for duration assets amid softening rate expectations. Housing (+1.79%) and net lease (+1.59%) rounded out the top half, while office (+1.15%) and retail (+1.13%) lagged but still finished green on balance.

Notable divergences deserve attention. AMT's +3.90% gain stood in stark contrast to UNIT's -2.26% decline, suggesting the tower trade is bifurcating on balance sheet quality. HPP's -4.09% print was the session's worst performer and a clear outlier against the office subsector's otherwise positive day, pointing to continued idiosyncratic West Coast office distress. AMH's +4.18% outperformance versus ELME's flat session highlights the single-family rental premium over multifamily workforce housing. WELL's -0.53% dip also diverged meaningfully from healthcare's +1.33% average.

Positioning into Tuesday should favor the momentum in hospitality and towers, particularly if the rate narrative holds. We would use HPP and UNIT weakness cautiously—these names need catalysts, not just mean reversion. Stay overweight quality duration beneficiaries.
